text:
Audit of Trailhead (Nuxt 4). The repo is small, so this covers everything in it.

## Critical

**1. `server/middleware/headers.ts:2-3` – `/guides` is sent with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.**
The middleware noindexes every path under `/guides`. That is your main content page, and it is listed in the sitemap. Google and most AI crawlers that honor this header will drop it.
Fix: delete the `/guides` check. If the intent was to block `/admin`, match `/admin` instead. `pages/admin.vue:2` already sets a meta noindex, so the header is redundant there.

**2. `nuxt.config.ts:2` – `ssr: false`.**
The site is a client-rendered SPA, so the served HTML is an empty shell. Most AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and similar) don't run JavaScript. They see no headings, text or links, and Google's indexing is slower and less reliable.
Fix: remove `ssr: false`, or at least use `routeRules: { '/**': { prerender: true } }` for a static site.

**3. `public/robots.txt:4` – relative sitemap URL.**
`Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` is invalid, because the spec requires an absolute URL.
Fix: `Sitemap: https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`.

## High

**4. `pages/index.vue:8` – the only link to `/guides` is a `<button>` with `router.push`.**
Crawlers don't click buttons or follow JS navigation, so `/guides` can't be discovered from the homepage.
Fix: `<NuxtLink to="/guides">Trail guides</NuxtLink>`, which renders a real `<a href>`. Remove the unused `useRouter` at line 2.

**5. `app.vue:2` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` – one global title and description for every page.**
`pages/index.vue` and `pages/guides.vue` set neither, so both pages share the title "Trailhead" and the description "Walking routes and trail guides." Duplicate titles and descriptions weaken ranking and the snippets shown in results.
Fix: call `useSeoMeta({ title, description })` in each page, and use a `titleTemplate` in `app.vue`.

**6. No canonical URLs, Open Graph or Twitter tags anywhere (`nuxt.config.ts:4-7`).**
There is no `<link rel="canonical">`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url` or `twitter:card`. Shared links and AI answer previews will be bare.
Fix: set `site.url` (for example via `@nuxtjs/seo`) or add these through `useSeoMeta` and `useHead`.

## Medium (GEO / content)

**7. `pages/guides.vue:3-4` and `pages/index.vue:7` – almost no content.**
The guides page has one sentence and no actual guides, routes, grades, distances or locations. There is nothing for search engines or AI systems to extract or cite.
Fix: add real route content, with one page per route such as `/guides/[slug]`. Use clear headings, short answer-style summaries, and facts like distance, grade and location.

**8. No structured data.**
There is no JSON-LD anywhere. Add `Organization` and `WebSite` on the homepage, and `Article`, `BreadcrumbList` or `Place` markup on guide pages. Use `useHead({ script: [{ type: 'application/ld+json', innerHTML: JSON.stringify(...) }] })`, or `nuxt-schema-org`.

**9. `public/sitemap.xml:3-4` – static, hand-maintained and on a placeholder domain.**
`trailhead.example` is not a real domain, and there are no `<lastmod>` values. Individual guide pages added later won't appear unless someone edits the file.
Fix: use `@nuxtjs/sitemap` to generate it from routes. Set the real production domain here and in the canonical, OG and robots.txt URLs.

**10. `public/robots.txt:1-2` – no AI crawler policy and no `llms.txt`.**
The blanket `User-agent: *` rule allows AI bots by default, which is fine if intended. It does not state a policy for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot or Google-Extended. There is also no `/llms.txt`.
Fix: add explicit rules for these bots, and optionally an `llms.txt` that summarizes the site and links the key pages.

## Low

- **`pages/admin.vue` is in the sitemap's blind spot but not in `robots.txt` consistently.** `Disallow: /admin` in `public/robots.txt:2` stops crawlers from fetching the page, so they never see its `noindex` meta. A disallowed URL can still appear in results if other sites link to it. Use one mechanism: either `noindex` (and allow crawling) or authentication.
- **`package.json`** – there are no SEO modules (`@nuxtjs/seo`, `@nuxt/image`) and no `generate` script for a static build. Adding them would cover items 5, 6, 8 and 9 with less hand-written code.
- **No favicon, `og:image` asset or `public/` images.** Add them for tab icons and for link previews.

## Suggested fix order
1. Remove the `/guides` noindex (`server/middleware/headers.ts`).
2. Turn SSR or prerendering back on (`nuxt.config.ts`).
3. Replace the button with `NuxtLink` (`pages/index.vue`).
4. Make the sitemap URL in `public/robots.txt` absolute.
5. Add per-page meta, canonical and OG tags.
6. Add real content and JSON-LD.

I haven't changed any files. I can apply the first four fixes if you want.
